current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2024, 2025 and 2026 (through 2026-08-20) via nysenate.gov consolidated laws and bill search. Codified Public Officers Law Article 6 (FOIL, §§ 84-90) available and current on nysenate.gov and on the DOS Committee on Open Government page (owner-supplied source doc NY_pol_article6_2026-08-20.txt, fetched 2026-08-20 from dos.ny.gov/coog/foil2.html). No 2024-2026 enacted amendment to the fee provisions of POL § 87(1) or § 89(3) was found; pending-only bills touching §§ 87/89 (2025 A950/S1418 attorney fees, S67 tabulations, S5847 COOG enforcement) are not law. The § 87(2)(j)/(k)/(n) vehicle-and-traffic photo exemptions repealed Dec 1, 2024 are non-fee provisions. GUIDANCE-VS-LAW GAP: the DOS consolidated page prints an older rendering of § 87(1)(b)(iii) ('the fees for copies of records...') WITHOUT the (1)/(2) subparagraph structure and WITHOUT the identical-record/6-month no-fee clause; the current nysenate.gov text (opened 2026-08-20) carries both — § 87(1)(b)(iii)(1) ('fees for paper copies of records shall not exceed twenty-five cents...') and (b)(iii)(2) (identical record prepared within past 6 months + electronic copy available = no fee) — confirming existing rule NY-0026's statutory anchor is current. Statutory fee architecture: § 87(1)(a)-(b) obliges each public corporation's governing body and each agency to set fees BY REGULATION under the 25-cent/9x14 ceiling and the § 87(1)(c) actual-cost components; the Committee on Open Government's general regulations, 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (§ 1401.8 Fees), opened on the official COOG page (opengovernment.ny.gov/freedom-information-law), expressly apply to state AND local agencies including counties, cities, towns, villages, school districts and fire districts — so Part 1401's figures are municipal authority, not an agency-only schedule. Minor reg/statute discrepancy: 21 NYCRR 1401.8(c)(i) says labor chargeable when 'more than two hours' is necessary, while POL § 87(1)(c)(iv) says no fee 'unless at least two hours' is needed — the statute governs.

resolutions.unit: USD per photocopy page (paper, not in excess of 9x14 inches)
resolutions.source_language: except when a different fee is otherwise prescribed by statute: (1) the fees for paper copies of records shall not exceed twenty-five cents per photocopy not in excess of nine inches by fourteen inches, or the actual cost of reproducing any other record in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (c) of this subdivision.
resolutions.notes: Ceiling, not a fixed rate: § 87(1)(b) requires each agency/public corporation to set its fee by regulation up to $0.25. FOIL 'agency' = any state or municipal department etc. (§ 86(3)); 21 NYCRR 1401.8(b)(1) applies the same ceiling expressly to local agencies and adds it 'shall not be construed to mandate the raising of fees' where an agency charged less. A different statutory fee overrides. State legislature (§ 88) and judiciary are outside this regime.

resolutions.unit: USD per photocopy page (any paper photocopy not in excess of 9x14 inches; statute does not distinguish color)
resolutions.source_language: except when a different fee is otherwise prescribed by statute: (1) the fees for paper copies of records shall not exceed twenty-five cents per photocopy not in excess of nine inches by fourteen inches, or the actual cost of reproducing any other record in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (c) of this subdivision.
resolutions.manual_verification: Neither POL § 87 nor 21 NYCRR 1401.8 distinguishes color from B&W; a color photocopy <=9x14 reads as a 'paper copy... per photocopy' under the same 25-cent ceiling. COOG advisory opinions on color copying were not opened this pass — confirm no opinion treats color as 'any other record' at actual cost.
resolutions.notes: No separate color rate exists in NY law; resolved as the same $0.25 ceiling by scope judgment (hence medium confidence). If a city treats color copies as 'any other record', the actual-cost components of § 87(1)(c) would govern instead.

resolutions.source_language: the fee for photocopies of records in excess of 9 x 14 inches shall not exceed the actual cost of reproduction
resolutions.notes: Oversized (>9x14) photocopies are capped at actual cost of reproduction (COOG regulation, binding on local agencies); the statute reaches the same result via 'the actual cost of reproducing any other record in accordance with... paragraph (c)'. The § 87(1)(c) component list (NY-0027..NY-0030, NY-9005) exclusively defines what 'actual cost' may include.

resolutions.basis: soft-standard ("actual cost of reproducing any other record")
resolutions.source_language: ...or the actual cost of reproducing any other record in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (c) of this subdivision, except when a different fee is otherwise prescribed by statute.
resolutions.notes: Photos, maps, transcripts and other non-photocopy media are 'any other record' — fee capped at actual cost with only the § 87(1)(c) components (lowest-paid qualified employee's hourly salary, storage media actual cost, qualifying outside-service cost). The 'different fee otherwise prescribed by statute' saver matters here: several record types (e.g., vital records, court transcripts) carry their own statutory fees outside FOIL.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6 (§§ 84-90); 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: searched POL art. 6 full text (owner-supplied DOS document + nysenate.gov § 87) and 21 NYCRR § 1401.8 (opened on the official COOG page). No graduated/volume page bands exist — a single flat 25-cent ceiling for <=9x14 paper photocopies and actual cost for everything else. A city may adopt tiers only beneath the flat ceiling.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: No free-page allowance per request exists in FOIL or Part 1401 (searched POL §§ 87/89 and 21 NYCRR 1401.8). Adjacent no-charge rules that are NOT a page allowance: inspection of records is free where no redaction is permitted (21 NYCRR 1401.8(a)(1), NY-9001); an identical record prepared within the past 6 months with an electronic copy available is free (POL § 87(1)(b)(iii)(2), NY-0026 — see item 'repeat').

resolutions.source_language: iv. preparing a copy shall not include search time or administrative costs, and no fee shall be charged unless at least two hours of agency employee time is needed to prepare a copy of the record requested.
resolutions.notes: Search labor is categorically non-chargeable — the item cannot exist. Statute excludes search time from 'actual cost'; 21 NYCRR 1401.8(a)(2) (binding on local agencies) states no fee for 'search for, administrative costs of, or employee time to prepare photocopies of records'. Verbatim clause quoted from the owner-supplied DOS Article 6 document.

resolutions.source_language: An agency shall not charge a fee for the following: ... (3) review of the content of requested records to determine the extent to which records must be disclosed or may be withheld;
resolutions.manual_verification: Edge: whether time spent performing electronic redactions counts as chargeable 'preparation' of a non-photocopy record (>=2h, lowest-paid-qualified-employee rate) rather than non-chargeable review — COOG advisory opinions on this line were not opened this pass.
resolutions.notes: Review-to-determine-disclosure is categorically non-chargeable for all state and local agencies (1401.8(a)(3)); paper redaction is handled by making a photocopy (1401.8(b)(3)) within the photocopy fee, with photocopy employee time also non-chargeable (1401.8(a)(2)). Any chargeable labor exists only as preparation of a non-photocopy record under the § 87(1)(c)(i) formula — see labor.billableWhen.

resolutions.basis: soft-standard (hourly salary of the lowest-paid employee with the necessary skill; no dollar figure in law)
resolutions.source_language: i. an amount equal to the hourly salary attributed to the lowest paid agency employee who has the necessary skill required to prepare a copy of the requested record;
resolutions.notes: No statutory dollar rate — the city supplies the wage of its lowest-paid qualified employee; chargeable only when the >=2-hour preparation threshold is met (NY-0028). § 89(3)(a): programming necessary to retrieve a record and transfer it to the requested medium 'shall not be deemed to be the preparation or creation of a new record' — so extraction/programming is FOIL work, billable only under this formula. 1401.8(d) requires electronic retrieval when it takes less employee time and allows the (c)(i)-(ii) fee for it.

resolutions.unit: hours of agency employee preparation time (per request; non-photocopy records only — never for search, review, administration, or photocopy labor)
resolutions.source_language: ...no fee shall be charged unless at least two hours of agency employee time is needed to prepare a copy of the record requested.
resolutions.manual_verification: Statute says 'at least two hours'; 21 NYCRR 1401.8(c)(i) says 'more than two hours'. The statute governs; the one-minute boundary difference should be noted to cities.
resolutions.notes: Labor is chargeable ONLY when >=2 hours of employee time is needed to prepare a copy of a non-photocopy ('any other') record. Never chargeable: search time, administrative costs (§ 87(1)(c)(iv)), review of content (1401.8(a)(3)), and employee time to prepare photocopies (1401.8(a)(2)) — i.e., paper-copy labor is never billable; the threshold applies to electronic/other-record preparation.

resolutions.source_language: c. In determining the actual cost of reproducing a record, an agency may include only: i. an amount equal to the hourly salary attributed to the lowest paid agency employee who has the necessary skill required to prepare a copy of the requested record;
resolutions.notes: No overhead or fringe surcharge can exist: § 87(1)(c) is an exclusive enumeration ('may include only') limited to hourly SALARY, storage media, and qualifying outside-service cost; § 87(1)(c)(iv) separately bars administrative costs. 21 NYCRR 1401.8 mirrors the exclusive list for local agencies.

Coverage note: searched POL § 87(1)(c) (full Article 6 text) and 21 NYCRR 1401.8. No billing time increment or rounding rule exists; the only time figure is the 2-hour chargeability/estimate threshold (separate items).

resolutions.source_language: ...no fee shall be charged unless at least two hours of agency employee time is needed to prepare a copy of the record requested.
resolutions.manual_verification: Once the 2-hour threshold is crossed, the statute does not say whether the first two hours are deducted or the entire preparation time is billable; COOG advisory opinions on this were not opened. Cities should confirm before billing hours 0-2.
resolutions.notes: NY has a 2-hour GATE, not a free-hours deduction: below 2 hours of preparation time, no labor fee at all; the statute is silent on deducting the first 2 hours once the gate opens. Engine shape: threshold gate (executed), not a freeLaborHours value. The gate figure itself is carried by labor.billableWhen.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: no TX § 552.275-style per-requestor periodic free personnel time exists anywhere in POL art. 6 or 21 NYCRR 1401 (both opened in full).

resolutions.unit: hours of agency employee time (OR: whenever an outside professional service would be retained, regardless of hours)
resolutions.source_language: A person requesting a record shall be informed of the estimated cost of preparing a copy of the record if more than two hours of an agency employee`s time is needed, or if an outside professional service would be retained to prepare a copy of the record.
resolutions.notes: Cost-estimate notice is mandatory above 2 hours of employee time or on any outside-service retention; the trigger is hours/retention, not a dollar amount. 21 NYCRR 1401.8(e) restates it for local agencies (duplicate of statute — no second rule row created).

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: no requester response window to a fee estimate (and no deemed-withdrawal on non-response) exists in POL art. 6 or 21 NYCRR 1401.8. City policy territory.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: no revised-estimate obligation keyed to a percentage overrun exists in POL art. 6 or 21 NYCRR 1401.8.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: no estimate validity/expiry period exists in POL art. 6 or 21 NYCRR 1401.8.

resolutions.source_authority: 21 NYCRR § 1401.8(f); N.Y. Pub. Off. Law § 89(3)(a) (searched for a threshold)
resolutions.source_language: An agency may require that the fee for copying or reproducing a record be paid in advance of the preparation of such copy.
resolutions.notes: No dollar threshold gates prepayment: NY law is silent on a deposit threshold — advance payment of the fee is permitted at ANY amount (1401.8(f), NY-9003; see payment.productionGate). A city choosing a threshold sets its own.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: no deposit cap percentage exists; 1401.8(f) allows requiring the (whole) fee in advance, i.e., up to 100%, with no partial-deposit scheme in law.

resolutions.source_language: An agency may require that the fee for copying or reproducing a record be paid in advance of the preparation of such copy.
resolutions.notes: Shape: pay-before-preparation is PERMITTED (discretionary), for all state and local agencies. Statutory backstop § 89(3)(a): 'Upon payment of, or offer to pay, the fee prescribed therefor, the entity shall provide a copy of such record' — production duty attaches on payment or offer to pay. Engine: optional prepayment gate before copy preparation/release.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: no statutory withdrawal-after-N-days or prior-debt prepayment rule exists in POL art. 6 or 21 NYCRR 1401. Practical consequence of nonpayment is only that the production duty never attaches (§ 89(3)(a) 'upon payment of, or offer to pay'). Lapse handling is city policy.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: FOIL's response clocks (§ 89(3)(a): 5 business days to respond; 20 business days from acknowledgment for disclosure or a date certain) contain no tolling/pause provision tied to an unpaid fee or deposit, and no grace period or lapse action. No statutory clock effect exists.

Coverage note: only the initial estimate notice exists (NY-0031 / rules.estimateNotifyThreshold). No rule requires a revised estimate on overrun, blocks collection above an estimate, or restarts any window.
out of scope per owner decision 2026-08-20 — finance-department policy, excluded from state rules profile

resolutions.basis: soft-standard (photocopies <=9x14 capped at $0.25/page; every other record capped at actual cost of reproduction with an exclusive component list)
resolutions.source_language: ...or the actual cost of reproducing any other record in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (c) of this subdivision. ... c. In determining the actual cost of reproducing a record, an agency may include only: ...
resolutions.notes: The request-level ceiling is structural: nothing above actual cost (components exclusively enumerated in § 87(1)(c)) may ever be charged, and paper photocopies are further capped at $0.25/page. No single dollar cap per request exists.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: no de-minimis dollar floor below which charging is barred. Related but distinct: categorical no-fee items (inspection, search, review, certification — NY-9001), the 6-month identical-record rule (NY-0026), and the discretionary waiver permission (1401.8(g), NY-9004) let a city not charge at any amount.

resolutions.source_authority: 21 NYCRR § 1401.8(b)(1); N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6 (searched)
resolutions.source_language: This section shall not be construed to mandate the raising of fees when an agency in the past has charged less than 25 cents for such copies;
resolutions.notes: No minimum fee exists anywhere in NY law; 1401.8(b)(1) affirmatively confirms agencies may keep charging LESS than the ceiling. Resolution is silent (no minimum provision), with the anti-minimum clause noted.

resolutions.basis: soft-standard ("actual cost of the storage devices or media provided")
resolutions.source_language: ii. the actual cost of the storage devices or media provided to the person making the request in complying with such request;
resolutions.notes: CD/DVD/USB chargeable only at the actual cost of the device actually provided — no fixed rates. Even in the free 6-month identical-record case, media actual cost survives (NY-0026). New rule NY-9005 gives § 87(1)(c)(ii) its own row (previously only embedded in NY-0026's exception).

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.manual_verification: COOG advisory opinions address postage charging in practice but were not opened this pass; confirm before a city adds a postage line item — postage is not among the § 87(1)(c) 'may include only' components.
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: no mail/handling/pickup charge provision exists in POL art. 6 or 21 NYCRR 1401.8. § 89(3)(b) requires accepting and answering email requests where reasonable means exist (email delivery effectively free). Note the exclusive § 87(1)(c) component list does not name postage.

resolutions.unit: USD per certification (no fee may be charged)
resolutions.source_language: An agency shall not charge a fee for the following: ... (4) any certification required pursuant to this Part.
resolutions.notes: FOIL certification (certifying a copy's correctness, § 89(3)(a) duty on request) is free for all state and local agencies. Caveat: 'except when a different fee is otherwise prescribed by statute' — certified copies under OTHER statutes (e.g., vital records, county clerk fee schedules) carry their own fees outside FOIL.

resolutions.basis: soft-standard ("actual cost of reproducing any other record"; components exclusively enumerated)
resolutions.source_language: ...or the actual cost of reproducing any other record in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (c) of this subdivision.
resolutions.notes: Audio/video are 'any other record': no per-recording, per-minute, or free-minutes figures exist. Chargeable components only: preparation labor (>=2h, lowest-paid-qualified rate), storage media actual cost, qualifying outside-service cost.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: no commercial-purpose fee schedule or surcharge exists — FOIL fees do not vary by requester purpose. The only purpose-sensitive rule is non-fee: § 89(3)(a) lets an agency require a written certification that lists of names/addresses will not be used for solicitation/fund-raising (and § 89(2)(b)(iii) makes such sale/release an unwarranted privacy invasion).

resolutions.source_language: An agency may waive a fee in whole or in part when making copies of records available.
resolutions.notes: Shape: waiver is a bare discretionary Permission (whole or part), for all state and local agencies — NO statutory grounds (no indigency/public-interest test), no purpose-statement requirement, no written-denial or waiver-specific appeal mechanics. Grounds and process are city policy. Statute itself is silent on waiver; the permission lives in the COOG regulation.

resolutions.source_authority: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6; 21 NYCRR Part 1401 (searched)
resolutions.notes: Coverage note: no fee-forfeiture-on-late-response rule exists. A late/failed response constitutes a denial for appeal purposes (§ 89(4)(a)) and can support attorney-fee awards in an Article 78 proceeding (§ 89(4)(c)) — remedies, not fee forfeiture.

resolutions.source_language: In the case where an identical record has been prepared for a previous request within the past 6 months and an electronic copy is available, an agency shall not charge a fee for the reproduction of such record, except for the actual cost of a storage device or media if one is provided to the requester in complying with such request.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (anchor confirmed on nysenate.gov § 87 text opened 2026-08-20; note the DOS consolidated page still prints the pre-amendment rendering without this clause)
resolutions.notes: Repeat-request rule: identical record prepared within the past 6 months + electronic copy available => $0 fee (media actual cost only). Engine shape: repeat-detection gate on the fee calculation (requestor-ledger lookback, 6 months). No aggregation threshold or multi-request fee aggregation rule exists in NY law.

new_rules.legal_concept: No fee for inspection, search, review, or certification (COOG regulation)
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency (state or local, including cities) shall not charge a fee for inspection of records where no redaction is permitted; for search, administrative costs, or employee time to prepare photocopies; for review of content to determine disclosure; or for any certification under Part 1401.
new_rules.trigger: Any FOIL request involving inspection, search, review, photocopy preparation, or certification
new_rules.source_language: Except when a different fee is otherwise prescribed by statute: (a) An agency shall not charge a fee for the following: (1) inspection of records for which no redaction is permitted; (2) search for, administrative costs of, or employee time to prepare photocopies of records; (3) review of the content of requested records to determine the extent to which records must be disclosed or may be withheld; or (4) any certification required pursuant to this Part.
new_rules.notes: COOG general regulations promulgated under POL § 89(1)(b)(iii) implementing § 87(1); Part 1401 expressly covers 'RECORDS OF STATE AND LOCAL AGENCIES, INCLUDING COUNTIES, CITIES, TOWNS, VILLAGES, SCHOOL DISTRICTS AND FIRE DISTRICTS' — municipal authority, unlike agency-specific parts (e.g., 21 NYCRR 9760.8). Adds beyond statute: photocopy employee time never chargeable; review never chargeable; certification free.

new_rules.legal_concept: Photocopy fee ceilings in the COOG regulation; no mandate to raise fees
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge for photocopies up to 25 cents per page (<=9x14 inches) and up to actual reproduction cost for photocopies over 9x14 inches; the regulation does not mandate raising fees where the agency historically charged less.
new_rules.trigger: Paper photocopies provided in response to a FOIL request
new_rules.source_language: (b) An agency may charge a fee for photocopies of records, provided that: (1) the fee shall not exceed 25 cents per page for photocopies not exceeding 9 by 14 inches. This section shall not be construed to mandate the raising of fees when an agency in the past has charged less than 25 cents for such copies; (2) the fee for photocopies of records in excess of 9 x 14 inches shall not exceed the actual cost of reproduction; or (3) an agency has the authority to redact portions of a paper record and does so prior to disclosure of the record by making a photocopy from which the proper redactions are made.
new_rules.notes: Restates the § 87(1)(b)(iii)(1) ceiling (NY-0024) with local scope explicit, and adds the anti-minimum clause and oversized actual-cost ceiling. Instrument row for the § 87(1)(a)-(b) delegation to COOG general regulations.

new_rules.legal_concept: Advance payment of copying fee may be required
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may require that the fee for copying or reproducing a record be paid in advance of preparing the copy.
new_rules.trigger: A copying/reproduction fee applies to the request
new_rules.source_language: An agency may require that the fee for copying or reproducing a record be paid in advance of the preparation of such copy.
new_rules.notes: No dollar threshold and no percentage cap — full prepayment may be required at any amount, at agency discretion. Binds/authorizes state and local agencies alike (Part 1401 scope).

new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may waive a fee in whole or in part when making copies of records available.
new_rules.trigger: Any fee otherwise chargeable for copies
new_rules.source_language: An agency may waive a fee in whole or in part when making copies of records available.
new_rules.notes: Bare permission — no grounds, no mandatory cases, no purpose statement, no written-denial or appeal mechanics specific to waiver anywhere in POL art. 6 or Part 1401. Waiver policy is left to the agency/city.

new_rules.atomic_rule: In determining actual reproduction cost, an agency may include the actual cost of the storage devices or media provided to the requester in complying with the request.
new_rules.trigger: A storage device or media (CD/DVD/USB etc.) is provided to the requester
new_rules.source_language: ii. the actual cost of the storage devices or media provided to the person making the request in complying with such request;
new_rules.notes: Gives § 87(1)(c)(ii) its own row (previously only referenced inside NY-0026's exception). Mirrored for local agencies at 21 NYCRR 1401.8(c)(ii). Actual cost of the device — no fixed media rates exist.

new_rules.legal_concept: Copy provided upon payment or offer to pay; free certification of correctness
new_rules.atomic_rule: Upon payment of, or offer to pay, the prescribed fee, the entity shall provide a copy of the record and shall certify to the correctness of the copy if so requested (or certify non-possession / not-found after diligent search).
new_rules.trigger: Requester pays or offers to pay the prescribed fee for a copy
new_rules.source_language: Upon payment of, or offer to pay, the fee prescribed therefor, the entity shall provide a copy of such record and certify to the correctness of such copy if so requested, or as the case may be, shall certify that it does not have possession of such record or that such record cannot be found after diligent search.
new_rules.notes: Statutory basis of the payment production gate: the copy-production duty attaches on payment OR offer to pay. Certification of correctness is a duty within the same clause and carries no fee (see 21 NYCRR 1401.8(a)(4), NY-9001).

new_rules.legal_concept: Mandatory electronic retrieval when less burdensome; fee limited to labor + media components
new_rules.atomic_rule: When an agency can retrieve or extract a record from a computer storage system with reasonable effort, or doing so takes less employee time than manual retrieval/redaction, it must do so electronically, and may then charge only the preparation-labor and storage-media components of actual cost.
new_rules.trigger: Requested record/data retrievable or extractable from a computer storage system
new_rules.source_language: When an agency has the ability to retrieve or extract a record or data maintained in a computer storage system with reasonable effort, or when doing so requires less employee time than engaging in manual retrieval or redactions from non-electronic records, the agency shall be required to retrieve or extract such record or data electronically. In such case, the agency may charge a fee in accordance with paragraph (c)(i) and (ii) above.
new_rules.source_authority: 21 NYCRR § 1401.8(d); see also N.Y. Pub. Off. Law § 89(3)(a)
new_rules.notes: Companion statutory clause (§ 89(3)(a)): programming necessary to retrieve and transfer a record 'shall not be deemed to be the preparation or creation of a new record'. Constrains labor.programming charges to the (c)(i)-(ii) components.

delegations_followed.statute_cite: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law § 87(1)(a)-(b) (rules 'pursuant to such general rules and regulations as may be promulgated by the committee on open government'); § 89(1)(b)(iii) (COOG shall 'promulgate rules and regulations with respect to the implementation of subdivision one... of section eighty-seven')
delegations_followed.instrument: Committee on Open Government general regulations, Public Access to Records of State and Local Agencies
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: No-fee categories (inspection w/o redaction, search/admin/photocopy labor, content review, certification); 25 cents/page ceiling <=9x14 with anti-minimum clause; actual-cost ceiling for oversized photocopies; labor component only when >2 hours (statute: at least 2 hours), lowest-paid qualified employee; storage-media actual cost; mandatory electronic retrieval; estimate notice trigger (2 hours / outside service); advance-payment permission; discretionary whole/part waiver.
delegations_followed.applies_to: all_public_bodies (Part 1401 heading: 'PUBLIC ACCESS TO RECORDS OF STATE AND LOCAL AGENCIES, INCLUDING COUNTIES, CITIES, TOWNS, VILLAGES, SCHOOL DISTRICTS AND FIRE DISTRICTS')

delegations_followed.statute_cite: N.Y. Pub. Off. Law § 87(1)(a)-(b) (each public corporation's governing body / each agency shall promulgate its own rules on 'the fees for copies of records' under the ceiling)
delegations_followed.instrument: Each municipality's own FOIL rules/regulations (city-level instrument)
delegations_followed.instrument_cite: n/a — municipality-specific; no statewide instrument exists
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: None extractable statewide by design: the operative per-city figure (e.g., the actual per-page fee at or under $0.25) lives in each city's own promulgated rules. This is the defers-to-city layer, bounded by the statute + Part 1401. Agency-specific examples supplied by owner (21 NYCRR 9760.8 LGAC; OTDA FOIL page) confirm the implement-by-regulation pattern but are NOT municipal authority per their CAUTION headers and were not cited for any value.

applicability_notes: FOIL 'agency' (§ 86(3)) = any state or municipal department, board, bureau, division, commission, committee, public authority, public corporation, council, office or other governmental entity, EXCEPT the judiciary and the state legislature — so every § 87/89 fee rule here binds municipalities and state agencies alike (applies_to = all_public_bodies).

21 NYCRR Part 1401 (COOG general regulations) expressly covers state AND local agencies including counties, cities, towns, villages, school districts and fire districts — it is municipal authority, unlike agency-specific NYCRR parts (e.g., 21 NYCRR 9760.8, LGAC-only, banked as illustration per its CAUTION header).
The state legislature runs a parallel fee regime under § 88(1)(c) (same 25-cent/9x14 ceiling, actual cost otherwise) — noted, out of municipal scope.

The 'except when a different fee is otherwise prescribed by statute' saver in § 87(1)(b)(iii) and 1401.8 means record-type-specific statutory fees (vital records, county clerk schedules, court transcripts) override the FOIL ceilings for those records.

§ 87(1)(b) is itself an express delegation to each public corporation/agency to set its operative fees by regulation under the ceilings — the city supplies the operative value for every 'ceiling'/'actual_cost_standard' item above.
